faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Can't find what you're looking for? Compare the plans, or create a free account and try it yourself.

free.a: Yes. The free plan has no time limit and doesn't need a credit card. Upgrade only when you need more links, custom domains, targeting or the API.

edit.q: Can I change where a link goes after I've shared it?
edit.a: Yes. Edit the destination whenever you like — the short link and any printed QR codes keep working and point to the new address right away.

openInApp.a: When someone taps a link to YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Spotify or another supported app on their phone, it opens in that app instead of the browser — so they're already signed in and one tap from following, watching or buying.

domain.q: Can I use my own domain?
domain.a: Yes, on paid plans. Point a subdomain such as go.yourbrand.com to us with a single CNAME record. HTTPS is set up and renewed automatically.

targeting.q: How is targeting different from a normal redirect?
targeting.a: A normal short link sends everyone to the same page. With targeting, rules look at the visitor's country, device, operating system, browser, language, referrer or the time of day, and send them to the destination you chose for them.

bots.a: No. Known bots and link-preview crawlers are recognised and left out of your numbers by default, so your analytics reflect real people.

teams.a: Yes. Create a team workspace, invite people by email and give them the owner, admin or member role. Everyone in the workspace shares links, domains and analytics.

api.a: Yes. Paid plans include the REST API and signed webhooks, so you can create links and react to clicks from your own systems.

faq.description: Straight answers about plans, limits and billing.

switch.a: Yes. Upgrade or downgrade from Billing at any time. Stripe prorates the difference on your next invoice, and higher limits apply right away.

limits.q: What happens when I reach a limit?
limits.a: Nothing breaks. Existing links keep redirecting, but you can't create more of that item until you upgrade or free up room. If you go over the monthly click allowance, redirects keep working and only the tracking of new clicks pauses until the next month.

yearly.a: You pay for twelve months up front at a lower price than twelve monthly payments. The cards show the yearly price as a monthly amount so you can compare.

payment.a: Payments are handled by Stripe, so we never see or store your card details. You can update your card and download invoices from Billing.

pooled.a: Limits belong to the person who pays. If you own several team workspaces, their usage counts toward the same plan.

downgrade.q: What if I cancel or downgrade?
downgrade.a: Your plan stays active until the end of the period you paid for. After that the account moves to Free: your data is kept, and anything above the Free limits becomes read-only.

info.destination: The page visitors reach when no targeting rule or A/B variant applies. Must be a full http(s) address.
info.domain: The domain the short link lives on. Add your own branded domain under Domains.
info.slug: The part after the domain, e.g. /spring-sale. Letters, numbers, dot, dash and underscore; it must be unique on the domain.
info.title: Your own label for the link. Also used as the page title in link previews and on cloaked pages.
info.folder: Groups related links in the list. Folders don't affect redirects.
info.description: Short summary used in link previews and on cloaked pages.
info.image: Shown when the short link is shared on social media or in messaging apps.
info.tags: Free-form labels for filtering and reporting. Separate with commas, up to 20.
info.iosDestination: iPhone and iPad visitors go here instead of the main destination, e.g. your App Store page or a universal link. Targeting rules and A/B tests still take priority.
info.androidDestination: Android visitors go here instead of the main destination, e.g. your Google Play page or an app link. Targeting rules and A/B tests still take priority.
info.openMode: Automatic: a normal redirect. Open in the app: on phones, links to YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, Spotify, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram or Pinterest try the app first. Leave in-app browsers: visitors inside Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and similar apps are offered the link in their real browser. Desktop visitors always get a normal redirect.
info.variant: One destination in the split. Visitors are assigned by weight and keep seeing the same variant.
info.weight: Relative share of traffic, 0–100. Weights of 70 and 30 send roughly 70% and 30% of visitors.
info.utmSource: Where the traffic comes from, e.g. newsletter or instagram. Added to the destination as utm_source.
info.utmMedium: The marketing channel, e.g. email, social or cpc.
info.utmTerm: The paid search keyword, if there is one.
info.utmContent: Tells links within one campaign apart, e.g. header-button and footer-link.
info.forwardQuery: Extra parameters on the short link, e.g. ?ref=partner, are copied to the destination. Parameters the destination already has are kept.
info.startsAt: The link goes live at this moment, in your local time. Until then visitors get the domain's not-found page and no clicks are counted.
info.expiresAt: After this moment the link stops sending visitors to the destination. In your local time.
info.expiredDestination: Where visitors go once the link has expired. Leave empty to treat the link as not found.
info.password: Visitors must enter this password before they are redirected. At least 8 characters.
info.cloak: Shows the destination inside a frame so the short URL stays in the address bar. Some sites refuse to be framed, and phones skip cloaking when an open mode applies.
info.noIndex: Asks search engines not to index or follow the short link. Recommended for most links.
info.archive: Archived links stop redirecting but keep their stats. You can unarchive them any time.
info.notes: Private notes for your team. Never shown to visitors.
info.when: What to check about the visitor: location, device, operating system, browser, language, where they came from, or the time.
info.operator: “Is one of” matches any listed value; “is not one of” matches everyone else, including visitors whose value is unknown.
info.referrerOperator: “Contains” looks for the text anywhere in the referring URL, “equals host” compares the referring domain exactly, and “is empty” matches visits without a referrer, such as typed URLs and many apps.
info.countries: Two-letter country codes, detected from the visitor's IP address. Separate with commas.
info.continents: Continent codes, detected from the visitor's IP address: EU Europe, NA North America, SA South America, AS Asia, AF Africa, OC Oceania, AN Antarctica.
info.regions: State or province names exactly as Cloudflare reports them, e.g. Istanbul or California.
info.languages: Matches the language ranked highest in the visitor's browser settings. Regional variants count as the main language, so British English matches English.
info.devices: Phone, tablet or desktop, detected from the browser's user agent.
info.operatingSystems: Detected from the user agent. iPads that request the desktop version of sites may show up as macOS.
info.browsers: Detected from the user agent. Pick browsers here and in-app browsers below; a visitor matches if either applies.
info.inAppBrowsers: Browsers built into social apps. They also match their engine above: Instagram on Android counts as Chrome too.
info.referrerValue: A domain such as google.com, or any part of the referring URL.
info.from: Start of the daily window, in the time zone next to it. If it is later than the end, the window runs past midnight.
info.to: End of the daily window, inclusive.
info.timezone: The IANA time zone the window is read in, e.g. Europe/Istanbul. The visitor's own time zone doesn't matter.
info.days: Weekdays the window applies to, in the chosen time zone.
info.priority: Lower numbers are checked first. The first rule whose conditions all match decides the destination.
info.sendTo: Where visitors matching every condition of this rule are sent.

bio.handleInfo: The unique path of your page, e.g. /acme. Letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores only. If you change it later, the old address stops working.
bio.domainInfo: The hostname your page is served on. Choose a verified custom domain for a branded address; the platform domain works right away.
bio.displayNameInfo: The big heading at the top of your page. Also used as the browser tab and share title when the SEO title is empty.
bio.bioInfo: A short intro under your name, up to 500 characters. Also used as the search and share description when the SEO description is empty.
bio.profileModeInfo: What appears above your name: a round photo, your logo, or large text such as initials. Only the selected one is shown.
bio.avatarInfo: Cropped to a circle, so use a square image with the face or subject centred. It is also the share image when none is set on the SEO tab.
bio.logoInfo: Shown instead of a photo, without cropping. A logo with a transparent background looks right on every theme.
bio.profileTextInfo: Large text shown in place of a photo, up to 40 characters — ideal for initials or a short brand name.
bio.coverInfo: Optional wide banner at the top of the page; your photo or logo overlaps its lower edge. A landscape image around 3:1 fits best.
bio.templatesInfo: Applies a ready-made mix of theme, colours, font and background in one click. It overwrites those design settings; your blocks and profile stay as they are.
bio.themeInfo: Base palette for the background, text and buttons. The colour fields under Background override individual parts of it.
bio.buttonStyleInfo: Shape and fill of every link button: solid, outline, soft tint or fully rounded pill.
bio.fontFamilyInfo: Typeface for all text on the page, including your name, bio and buttons.
bio.bgTypeInfo: Theme keeps the palette's own background. Solid colour, gradient or image replace it — only the type selected here is used.
bio.bgColorValueInfo: Page background as a hex colour such as #111111. Pick it with the swatch or type the code.
bio.bgGradientValueInfo: Any CSS gradient, e.g. linear-gradient(135deg, #0f766e, #111827). Up to 400 characters.
bio.bgImageInfo: Covers the whole page behind your content and is cropped to fit the screen. Pick a calm image so text stays readable.
bio.buttonColorInfo: Fill and border colour of link buttons. Leave empty to use the theme's colour.
bio.buttonTextColorInfo: Colour of the text on link buttons. Make sure it contrasts with the button colour; empty uses the theme.
bio.textColorInfo: Colour of your name, bio and text blocks. Leave empty to use the theme's colour.
bio.customCssInfo: CSS declarations applied to the page itself, e.g. font-size: 17px; letter-spacing: .02em; border-radius: 24px. Selectors, @ rules and unsupported properties are dropped silently.
bio.adsEnabledInfo: Shows your own promo images around the page — your campaigns, not third-party ads. Turn it off to hide them without deleting the images.
bio.adMobileInfo: Shown above your profile on phones and tablets, hidden on wide screens. A wide landscape image works best.
bio.adLeftInfo: Pinned to the left edge on desktop screens only, about 176 px wide. Use a tall portrait image. Not shown in the live preview.
bio.adRightInfo: Pinned to the right edge on desktop screens only, about 176 px wide. Use a tall portrait image. Not shown in the live preview.
bio.adHrefInfo: Where a click on this banner goes; it opens in a new tab. Leave empty to show the image without a link.
bio.publishedInfo: Switches the page on or off for visitors. On a saved page it applies instantly without pressing Save, and switching it on clears any schedule.
bio.publishAtInfo: Keeps the page hidden until this moment even while Published is on, then it goes live by itself. Switch Published on first, then pick the date and save.
bio.unpublishAtInfo: The page switches itself off at this moment and visitors get a 404 — handy for time-limited campaigns. Leave empty to stay live.
bio.sensitiveInfo: Shows a warning screen first; visitors tap Continue to see the page. Use it for age-restricted or sensitive content.
bio.passwordInfo: Visitors must enter this password before the page loads. It is stored hashed, so it can't be shown again — only replaced or removed.
bio.removePasswordInfo: Removes the password gate when you save, so anyone with the link can open the page again.
bio.seoTitleInfo: Title shown in search results, the browser tab and link previews on social apps. Up to 120 characters; empty uses the display name.
bio.seoDescriptionInfo: Summary under the title in search results and share previews. Up to 300 characters; empty uses your bio.
bio.ogImageInfo: Picture shown when the page link is shared on WhatsApp, X, LinkedIn and similar apps. 1200×630 px works best; empty uses the avatar.
bio.labelInfo: Text on the button, up to 120 characters. Short, action-led labels such as "Shop the collection" get more taps.
bio.destinationInfo: The web address the button opens, e.g. https://acme.com/shop. If you leave out https://, it is added for you.
bio.iconInfo: Optional small square image before the label, such as a product thumbnail. It takes priority over the built-in icon.
bio.emphasisInfo: Highlighted adds a lifted shadow so this button stands out. Use it for one or two key links only.
bio.iconNameInfo: Built-in icon shown before the label when no image is uploaded — e.g. a cart for a shop link.
bio.newTabInfo: New tab keeps your bio page open behind the destination; same tab replaces it. New tab is the usual choice for external sites.
bio.platformInfo: Sets the icon shown in the row. Email opens the visitor's mail app; WhatsApp also accepts a phone number.
bio.urlOrHandleInfo: Paste a profile link or just the username (e.g. acme or @acme) — usernames are turned into the right profile link for the platform. For Email enter the address; for WhatsApp a number with country code.
bio.bodyInfo: Free text up to 2,000 characters. Line breaks are kept; links and formatting are not supported.
bio.alignmentInfo: Centre suits short statements; left is easier to read for longer paragraphs.
bio.headingInfo: A section title that splits your page into groups, e.g. "Latest videos". Up to 120 characters.
bio.imageInfo: Shown at full block width. Any aspect ratio works; landscape images need less scrolling on phones.
bio.altTextInfo: Read aloud by screen readers and shown if the image can't load. Describe what the image shows rather than writing "image of".
bio.linksToInfo: Makes the image clickable, e.g. a campaign banner that opens a landing page. https:// is added if you leave it out.
bio.providerInfo: The service the player comes from. It must match the link you paste next to it.
bio.shareUrlInfo: The normal page link, e.g. youtube.com/watch?v=… or open.spotify.com/track/…. It is turned into an embedded player automatically.
bio.formModeInfo: Email capture saves addresses under Leads, where you can export them as CSV. WhatsApp opens a chat with your number, pre-filled with the visitor's message; nothing is stored.
bio.formButtonInfo: Text on the submit button, up to 40 characters, e.g. "Subscribe" or "Message us".
bio.formTitleInfo: A line above the form telling visitors what they get, e.g. "Get our monthly newsletter".
bio.formWhatsappInfo: Your WhatsApp number in international format with country code, e.g. +905551112233. The chat opens with this number.
bio.formSuccessInfo: Message shown after a visitor submits their email, up to 200 characters. Leave empty for a default thank-you.

qr.logoErrorAuto: Error correction is set to the highest level (H) automatically, so the code still scans.
qr.logoLargeBody: Even with the highest error correction, a logo wider than 25% of the code can stop some phones from reading it. Make it smaller, or test with a few phones before printing.
qr.stepFrameDesc: A frame with a short call to action gets more scans.
qr.frameTextHint: {count}/{max} characters. Short and clear works best.
qr.frameColourHint: When off, the frame uses the dot colour.
qr.frameContrastTitle: The frame text may be hard to read
qr.frameContrastBody: The frame colour is too close to the background. Pick a darker frame colour.
qr.stepExportDesc: Get the file for print or screen. Downloads always match the saved design.
qr.exportLockedTitle: Create the code to download it
qr.exportLockedBody: As soon as it's created you can download it as PNG, SVG or PDF — here and from your QR list.
qr.pdfPrintSize: Prints about {cm} cm wide at 300 dpi.
qr.sizeHintMedium: Good for slides, social posts and small prints.
qr.sizeHintLarge: For posters, packaging and large prints.
qr.unsavedDownloadBody: We'll save them first, so the file matches the preview.
qr.exportAdvancedDesc: The size used by quick downloads from your QR list.
qr.deleteConfirmDesc: “{name}” will be removed from your QR codes.
qr.deleteBulletStatic: Printed copies keep working — their content is stored in the code itself.
qr.deleteTemplateDesc: “{name}” will be removed for everyone in this workspace. Codes that used it keep their look.
qr.saveTemplateIncludes: Saves the colours, shape, logo, frame and caption — not what the code opens.
qr.templatesEmpty: Save your current colours, shape and logo as a template to reuse on the next code.
qr.saveTemplateDesc: Reuse this look on your next codes with one click.
qr.qualityFailAdvice: Foreground and background are too close in brightness. Darken one of them.
qr.qualityLowAdvice: Readable up close, but likely to fail on a poster or in dim light.
qr.qualityInvertedAdvice: Light modules on a dark background — some older scanners refuse these.
qr.filteredEmptyTitle: No QR codes for this link
qr.filteredEmptyDesc: Design one now — it will encode this short link, so you can re-target it later without reprinting.

linkCard.emptyDesc: Create a printable code for this link in one click. You can restyle it in the designer at any time.
linkCard.moreCodes: {count, plural, one {# code points} other {# codes point}} at this link.

info.name: Only your team sees this name. It labels the code in your QR list and in downloads, and is not encoded in the code.
info.payloadKind: Short link codes are dynamic: change the destination later and every printed copy follows, with scans counted. The other types write their content straight into the code and cannot change after printing.
info.shortLink: The code opens this short link. Scans show up in the link's statistics as QR scans.
info.payloadUrl: Written into the code as-is, so it cannot be re-targeted or tracked. Use a short link if you might need to change it later.
info.vcardName: Full name saved to the phone's contacts when the code is scanned.
info.vcardOrg: Company or organisation shown under the name. Optional.
info.vcardPhone: Include the country code, e.g. +44 20 7946 0000, so the number also works from abroad.
info.vcardEmail: Email address added to the contact card. Optional.
info.vcardUrl: Website added to the contact card — your site or a profile page. Optional.
info.wifiSsid: The network name exactly as devices show it. It is case-sensitive.
info.wifiPassword: Anyone who scans the code can read this password. Leave it empty for open networks.
info.wifiSecurity: Match your router's setting. Most networks use WPA/WPA2; pick Open only for networks without a password.
info.wifiHidden: Turn on if the network does not broadcast its name, so phones know to look for it.
info.caption: Short text printed under the code, such as a call to action. It is part of the image, not of the encoded data.
info.templates: Reusable looks for this workspace: colours, shape, logo, frame and caption. Applying one never changes what the code opens.
info.palettes: Colour pairs with enough contrast to scan reliably — a safe starting point.
info.foreground: Colour of the modules (the dots). Keep it much darker than the background so the code scans reliably.
info.background: Colour behind the modules and around the code. Light colours scan best.
info.tintFinders: Gives the three large corner squares their own colour. Keep it dark: scanners use these squares to find the code.
info.cornerColour: Colour of the three corner squares. It needs the same strong contrast with the background as the foreground.
info.moduleShape: Look of the small modules. Every shape scans; square is the most robust on low-quality prints.
info.errorCorrection: How much of the code can be scratched or covered and still scan. Higher levels make the pattern denser.
info.quietZone: Blank border around the code, in modules. Scanners need at least 2; use 4 for print.
info.exportSize: Width in pixels used when you download from the QR list. In step 5 you can pick a size for each download.
info.logo: Put your own image, a brand icon or an emoji in the centre. Error correction switches to H so the code still scans.
info.logoSize: Logo width as a share of the code. A larger logo hides more data; stay under 25% for reliable scans.
info.pngSize: Width of the file in pixels. Bigger files print sharper; 1024 px is plenty for screens.
info.templateName: A name to recognise this style in the template list. Only your workspace sees it.
info.frame: Draws a border around the code with a short call to action. It is part of the image and doesn't change what the code opens.
info.frameText: A few words shown in the frame, such as “Scan me”. Up to 24 characters.
info.frameColour: Colour of the frame and its label. When off, it matches the dot colour.
info.fileFormat: PNG is an image for screens, SVG stays sharp at any size, and PDF is ready to print.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.description: From a blank workspace to a live short link you can share.
gettingStarted.stepsTitle: Four steps to your first link

account.title: Create your account
account.body: Sign up with your email and confirm the address from the link we send. Every account gets a personal workspace on the free plan; upgrade from Billing when you need custom domains, targeting or API access.

domain.title: Choose where links live
domain.body: Every link belongs to a domain. Use the platform domain out of the box, or add your own under Domains once your plan includes custom hostnames.

link.title: Create a link
link.body: Open Links → New link, paste the long URL, pick the domain and optionally set a custom slug. Advanced options — password, expiry, routing rules — can be added now or later.

share.title: Share and measure
share.body: Copy the short URL or download a QR code. Clicks appear on the Dashboard within seconds; open a link’s Stats tab for full breakdowns.

tip.title: Team workspaces
tip.body: Paid plans can create team workspaces. Members share links, domains and analytics but keep their own sign-ins; admins manage API keys and webhooks, and the person who pays manages billing.

gettingStarted.nextRouting: Country, device and language rules, open-in-app and A/B splits.
gettingStarted.nextApi: Create links from your own code.

links.title: Links
links.description: Short links are the core of the product. This guide covers creating them, every option on the link screen and day-to-day management.
links.createBody: Each link maps a slug on a domain to a destination URL. When someone opens it, the redirect service looks up the hostname and slug, applies your rules and sends the visitor on.

createSteps.0: Go to Links and click New link.
createSteps.1: Paste the destination URL. Missing schemes are added for you, and unsafe destinations (malware, phishing, non-web schemes) are refused.
createSteps.2: Pick the domain and, if you like, a custom slug. Leave the slug empty for a random 7-character one.
createSteps.3: Save. The short URL is ready to copy immediately.

links.optionsBody: Open any link from the list to change these. Edits apply to new visits within seconds; the short URL never changes.

slug.label: Custom slug
slug.desc: Replace the random code with a readable path like /launch. Letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores; 3–5 character slugs need a paid plan.

password.label: Password
password.desc: Visitors enter a password (8+ characters) before the redirect runs. Needs a plan with password protection.

expiry.label: Expiry
expiry.desc: Stop redirecting after a date. Send expired visits to another URL, or they get the domain's not-found page.

schedule.label: Start date
schedule.desc: Keep the link inactive until a date — useful for launches.

utm.label: UTM parameters
utm.desc: Adds utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term and utm_content to the destination. UTM values already on the visit win.

forward.label: Forward query
forward.desc: Passes other query parameters from the short URL through to the destination.

devices.label: iOS / Android destinations
devices.desc: Send iPhone and Android visitors to a store or app page when no targeting rule matched.

openMode.label: Open in app
openMode.desc: Open YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and other supported destinations in their app, or escape in-app browsers. See Smart routing.

tags.label: Tags
tags.desc: Free-form labels (up to 20) for filtering in the list and the API.

cloak.label: Cloaking
cloak.desc: Keeps the short URL in the address bar and shows your own title, description and image in link previews; the destination loads inside the page. Business plan and above.

links.organizeBody: Group campaign links in folders and label them with tags. Archive links you no longer promote: they stop redirecting (visitors get the domain's not-found page) but their analytics history stays.
links.bulkBody: Select several links in the list to work on them at once.

bulkItems.0: Archive, move to a folder, tag, duplicate or delete a selection in one go.
bulkItems.1: Import up to 1,000 links from CSV (slug, destination, title, tags, folder, open_mode) and export up to 50,000.
bulkItems.2: Rewrite destinations: replace one host with another across links, device destinations, rules and A/B variants, with a preview first. Admins only.

links.relatedRouting: Smart routing — country, device and A/B rules

qrCodes.title: QR codes
qrCodes.description: Turn any link or payload into a downloadable, brand-styled QR code.
qrCodes.createBody: A QR code can point at one of your short links (so you can change the destination later) or encode a fixed URL, contact card or Wi‑Fi network.

createSteps.0: Open QR codes → New QR code.
createSteps.1: Choose the type and fill in the fields.
createSteps.2: Pick colours, dot style, an optional logo and a caption under the code, then save. Save the style as a template to reuse it.

qrCodes.payloadBody: Link codes inherit targeting, open-in-app and analytics from the short link they point at.
qrCodes.dynamicBody: Link codes encode the short URL, not the destination. Change where the link goes at any time and every printed copy follows — and scans show up in analytics as QR scans.

rows.linkDesc: Trackable codes tied to an existing short link.
rows.urlDesc: One-off codes that encode a fixed URL.
rows.vcardDesc: Share name, phone and email when scanned.
rows.wifiDesc: Let guests join a network from a poster or menu.

qrCodes.designBody: Style is yours, but a code has to scan on every phone. Keep these in mind:

designTips.0: Keep a quiet zone (margin) around the code — do not crop it flush to artwork.
designTips.1: Prefer dark modules on a light background with strong contrast; inverted codes fail on some scanners.
designTips.2: Adding a logo raises error correction automatically. Test on paper at the size you plan to print, not just on screen.

qrCodes.exportBody: Download any code as SVG for print, or PNG and PDF from 128 to 4096 pixels. Logos need a plan with QR logos.

bioPages.title: Bio pages
bioPages.description: A hosted, mobile-first link-in-bio page on our short domain or your own.
bioPages.handleBody: Each bio page has a handle that becomes its address: {host}/yourhandle on the platform domain, or go.yourbrand.com/yourhandle on one of your custom domains. Handles of 3–5 characters need a paid plan.
bioPages.blocksBody: Stack blocks to build the page and drag to reorder them. A page holds up to 100 blocks.

blocks.0: Links — buttons to any URL, with an icon, a highlight or opening in a new tab.
blocks.1: Social icons — up to 12 profiles such as Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, X, LinkedIn and WhatsApp.
blocks.2: Headers and text — section titles, short bios or announcements.
blocks.3: Images and embeds — pictures, YouTube, Spotify and Vimeo players.
blocks.5: Forms — collect emails, or start a WhatsApp chat (needs a plan with bio forms).

bioPages.lookBody: Start from a theme, then change the button style, font, background (colour, gradient or image), profile photo or logo and cover image. Paid plans can remove the platform branding and add custom CSS.
bioPages.publishBody: A page stays private until you publish it. You can also schedule when it goes live and when it comes down, protect it with a password, and set its SEO title, description and share image.
bioPages.leadsBody: When a form block collects emails, submissions appear under the page's Leads tab, where you can export them as CSV.
bioPages.statsBody: Bio views are counted separately from link clicks. Open Stats on a bio page to see views over time and top outbound links.

domains.title: Custom domains
domains.description: Serve short links and bio pages from your own hostname, with HTTPS set up for you.

add.title: Add the hostname
add.body: Under Domains → Add domain, enter a dedicated subdomain such as go.acme.com. Hostnames starting with www. are not accepted.

dns.title: Point DNS
dns.body: Create the CNAME record (and the TXT record for the certificate) shown in the panel at your DNS provider. On Cloudflare, connect your account and the records are created for you.

verify.title: Wait for verification
verify.body: Once DNS propagates, the certificate is issued and the domain becomes active. The Domains page shows the status and what is still missing.

default.title: Set as default
default.body: Mark one domain as default so new links pre-select it in the editor.

domains.dnsBody: The record points your hostname at our edge. If you use Cloudflare, leave the proxy off (grey cloud) for this record.
domains.rootBody: Choose where visitors go when they open the bare domain, and where unknown, expired or archived slugs send people. Without these they see the platform's not-found page.
domains.sslBody: Certificates renew automatically as long as the CNAME stays. Removing or changing it pauses renewal and eventually breaks HTTPS for every link on the domain.

routing.title: Smart routing
routing.description: One short link can send each visitor to a different destination based on context.
routing.howBody: Every visit is checked before the redirect, in this order:

order.0: Expiry and start date — a link outside its window goes to the expired destination or the not-found page.
order.1: Targeting rules, in priority order. A rule matches when all of its conditions match; the first match wins.
order.2: A/B split — if the link has variants, the visitor gets one by weight and keeps it on later visits.
order.3: The main destination, or the iOS / Android destination for phones when nothing above matched.
order.4: Finally UTM tags and forwarded query parameters are added, and open-in-app or cloaking is applied.

routing.conditionsBody: Each rule combines up to 20 conditions. Most accept “is one of” or “is not one of” a list of values.

rows.geoEx: Country is TR → Turkish pricing page
rows.deviceEx: Device is mobile or tablet → mobile landing page
rows.osEx: OS is iOS → App Store listing; Android → Google Play
rows.browserEx: Opened inside Instagram or TikTok → a page built for in-app browsers
rows.languageEx: Browser language is de → German landing page
rows.abEx: Split 50/50 between two URLs to compare them (separate from rules)

routing.priorityBody: Rules run top to bottom, so put the most specific first — for example “Germany and desktop” above a broad “Germany” rule. Reorder them in the link editor. Targeting needs a plan with targeting; A/B splits need A/B testing.
routing.appsBody: Phones open most links in a browser, where people are not signed in to the app they need. The open mode fixes that per link, on every plan:

appsTable.app: On iOS and Android, supported destinations open in their native app. Android goes straight to the app and falls back to the web if it is missing; iOS shows a one-tap “Open in app” page.
appsTable.browser: When the visit comes from an in-app browser (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook…), try to reopen the destination in the phone's real browser, with a copy-link fallback.

routing.appsList: YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, Spotify, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram and Pinterest. Other destinations, desktop visitors and bots always get a normal redirect.
routing.exampleBody: When creating or updating a link through the REST API, send rules, abVariants and openMode alongside the destination:
routing.mobileBody: Set iosDestination and androidDestination for simple store routing without writing rules. They apply only when no targeting rule or A/B variant matched, so a rule can still override them.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Understand who clicked, from where and on what device.
analytics.dashboardBody: The dashboard adds up clicks and visitors across all links for the selected range, compared with the previous period. Top links and recent activity help you spot spikes quickly; Analytics has the full breakdowns.
analytics.linkBody: Every link has a Stats tab with the same breakdowns scoped to that link, including which targeting rule or A/B variant each visit got. Bio pages have their own Stats tab.

rows.clicksDesc: Every redirect, including repeat visits by the same person.
rows.visitorsDesc: Distinct visitors, counted with a privacy-friendly token that rotates daily — exact within a day, an estimate across longer ranges.
rows.scansDesc: Visits that came through one of your QR codes, counted separately from ordinary clicks.
rows.bioDesc: Views of your bio pages and taps on the links inside them.
rows.referrerDesc: The site or app that sent the visitor.
rows.countryDesc: Country, region and city, derived from the IP address — approximate.
rows.deviceDesc: Phone, tablet or desktop, plus operating system, browser and browser language.
rows.utmDesc: utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign of each visit.

analytics.botsBody: Known bots and link-preview crawlers still get redirected (so previews work) but are excluded from your numbers and never sent to webhooks.
analytics.rangesBody: Choose the last 24 hours, 7, 30 or 90 days, 12 months, all time or a custom range. How far back you can go depends on the analytics history included in your plan (see Billing).
analytics.exportBody: Use the Export menu on Analytics or a link's Stats tab to download the time series as CSV or every breakdown as JSON. Through the API, GET /analytics and GET /links/{id}/stats return the same data.

api.title: REST API
api.description: Programmatic access to links, QR codes, bio pages, domains and analytics.
api.authBody: Every request needs a workspace API key. Workspace admins create keys in Settings → API on plans that include API access; the full key is shown exactly once.

authTable.scopeValue: One workspace — the key inherits plan limits and quotas.

api.keysBody: Create named keys per environment. Revoke immediately if a key leaks — there is no undo.
api.baseBody: All paths below are relative to:
api.rateBody: Each key has an hourly request allowance set by your plan. Every response carries x-ratelimit-limit, x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset (Unix seconds); past the limit you get 429 rate_limited until the window resets.
api.exampleBody: POST /links with domainId and destination. Omit slug to get a random one. Optional fields include title, tags, folderId, expiresAt, password, utm, iosDestination, androidDestination, openMode, rules and abVariants.
api.errorsBody: Errors return JSON with a stable code and a readable message. Validation errors also list the failing fields.

rows.missing: No x-api-key or Authorization header was sent.
rows.invalid: The key is wrong, malformed or revoked.
rows.plan: Your plan does not include API access.
rows.quota: A plan limit was reached, or the request uses a feature your plan does not include (targeting, passwords, custom CSS…).
rows.noAccess: The key's workspace cannot use this resource.
rows.validation: The body failed validation — see error.fields.
rows.json: The body is not valid JSON.
rows.slugTaken: That slug is already taken on this domain.
rows.notFound: The resource does not exist in this workspace.
rows.rate: Hourly limit exceeded — check the x-ratelimit-* headers.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Push link and bio events to your backend the moment they happen.
webhooks.setupBody: Register a public HTTPS URL and choose which events it receives. Each endpoint gets its own signing secret, shown once when you create it. Webhooks need a plan that includes them and the admin role.
webhooks.settingsBody: In Settings → Webhooks you can pause and resume an endpoint, send a test event, replay the last delivery and see the most recent attempts. To change a secret, delete the endpoint and add it again.
webhooks.eventsBody: Every delivery is a JSON POST. The event name is in the body and in the x-short-event header.
webhooks.payloadBody: The body is always { event, createdAt, data }. For link.created and link.updated, data is the full link as the API returns it; click and view events carry the visit details below.

rows.link_created: A link is created in the panel or through the API.
rows.link_updated: Any field of a link changes, including its destination or rules.
rows.link_clicked: A person opens a short link or scans a QR code (bots are never sent). Arrives a few seconds after the click.
rows.biopage_viewed: A person views a published bio page.
rows.domain_verified: A custom domain's DNS and HTTPS certificate are active.
rows.link_broken: Two health checks in a row found the destination down (404/410/5xx, DNS failure or timeout).

webhooks.signatureBody: Each delivery carries x-short-signature: t=timestamp,v1=signature. Compute HMAC-SHA256 with your signing secret over the timestamp, a dot and the raw request body (t.body), then compare the hex digest with v1 in constant time. Reject mismatches and timestamps older than a few minutes.
webhooks.deliveryBody: Respond with a 2xx status within 8 seconds. Timeouts, network errors, 429 and 5xx responses are retried — three attempts in total, a second or so apart. Other responses, including redirects (which are not followed), count as final.

deliveryTips.0: Return 200 quickly and do the real work in the background.
deliveryTips.1: Deliveries are best-effort and can arrive twice or out of order; make your handler idempotent.
deliveryTips.2: Paused endpoints receive nothing until you resume them.
deliveryTips.3: Store the signing secret somewhere safe; it cannot be read again from the panel.
